label: rem:hopf-ring-rigidity
title: Crossing-energy efficiency and rigidity of the Hopf ring
html:
Remark. Crossing-energy efficiency and rigidity of the Hopf ring

Crossing energy of the ring. The crossing energy is determined by the Alexander polynomial evaluated at the substrate parameter:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathcal{R}_N)
   \propto 
  \Delta_{T(2,N)}(q).

Contrast with the pairwise picture. A naïve pairwise ring has crossing energy proportional to N. The threading link evaluates to roughly N/2. The threading is topologically more efficient.

Structure Binding Alexander weight Crossings
Chain (N-1 Hopf links) pairwise N - 1 2(N-1)
Ring (N Hopf links) pairwise N 2N + rearrangement
Ring (T(2,N) threading) non-local \Delta_{T(2,N)}(q) \approx N/2 2(N-1)

The threading ring has fewer crossings than the pairwise ring and no rearrangement cost.

Rigidity. The threading link passes through every atom twice. Deforming the ring requires moving the threading link through all N atoms simultaneously. This global operation is the topological origin of ring rigidity.
